entities.summary: Symphony Center is a music complex located at 220 South Michigan Avenue in the Loop area of Chicago, Illinois. Home to the Chicago Symphony Orchestra (CSO); Chicago Symphony Chorus; Civic Orchestra of Chicago; and the Institute for Learning, Access, and Training; Symphony Center includes the 2,522-seat Orchestra Hall, which dates from 1904; Buntrock Hall, a rehearsal and performance space named for the CSO trustee and benefactor Dean L. Buntrock; Grainger Ballroom, an event space overlooking Michigan Avenue and the Art Institute of Chicago; a public multi-story rotunda; Forte, a restaurant and café; and administrative offices.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Symphony Center is significant because it has been home to the Chicago Symphony Orchestra since its founding in 1891 and continues to be a major cultural institution in Chicago, hosting over 200 performances annually. Its legacy can be seen in the numerous young musicians trained by the Civic Orchestra of Chicago.
